title: Transport handbook: connection & timeout levers with language-specific examples
creator: Amina Patel
description: Create a practical, implementable handbook for SDK authors and integrators describing recommended default transport settings (timeouts, connection pooling, keep-alive, TLS session reuse) and streaming ergonomics with concrete examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go. This ticket consolidates experiments, field telemetry, and regression guardrails so that each SDK ships sensible defaults that reduce connection churn, improve tail latency, and make streaming APIs resilient without requiring customers to deep-dive into socket plumbing.
motivation: We see customer reports and internal telemetry showing high socket churn, elevated tail latency on cold connections, and frequent user errors when callers combine short per-request deadlines with long-lived streaming calls. Unifying guidance will reduce support noise, cut per-request token cost by enabling connection reuse/keepalive, and make SDK behavior predictable across languages.
out_of_scope: Changing server-side SLOs, wholesale network stack rewrites, or per-customer tuned presets (this ticket only defines defaults and examples; dedicated/reserved offerings will have separate guidance).
proposed_solution: Publish an SDK-agnostic section of levers, then provide concrete snippet-level recommendations for Python, TypeScript, and Go. Levers include: 1) three-tier deadline model (client deadline, per-attempt timeout, idle/lease timeout), 2) adaptive connection pool sizing by concurrency and route affinity, 3) TCP/TLS keepalive and session reuse best-practices, 4) streaming-specific early-deadline handling and reconnect semantics, 5) retry and hedging interactions with long polling/streaming. Provide default numeric values derived from telemetry and lab tests and show how to override per-route.
decision_points: Default per-request overall deadline: 60s vs 120s (we propose 60s for interactive, 120s for batch via explicit config)
Per-attempt transport timeout (for hedging/retries): 20s recommended to avoid long blocking backoffs
Connection pool size heuristic: min(8, max(2, ceil(parallel_requests/2))) with route affinity option
Enable TCP keepalive by default at SDK level with OS fallback rather than requiring platform metrics to be present
Streaming reconnect policy: attempt 1 immediate reconnect on transient errors, exponential backoff thereafter up to 30s, preserve in-flight prefix cache when resumed if server supports resume token
examples:
Python - httpx + asyncio: 
- transport config: httpx.HTTPTransport(windowed_keepalive=True)
- defaults: connect_timeout=2.0, read_timeout=20.0, overall_deadline=60.0
- pool: max_connections=16, max_keepalive=16
- streaming: set stream_chunk_timeout=5.0 and use async iterator with graceful backoff and resume token handling
Snippet: client = RedwoodClient(transport=Transport(connect_timeout=2, read_timeout=20, pool_max=16), overall_deadline=60)

TypeScript - fetch/undici: 
- transport config: Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 32, maxFreeSockets: 8 })
- defaults: connectTimeoutMs=2000, responseTimeoutMs=20000, overallTimeoutMs=60000
- streaming: prefer ReadableStream with per-chunk deadline of 3s and a streaming-watcher that raises specific StreamTimeout error for caller ergonomics
Snippet: const client = new RedwoodClient({ agent: new Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 32 }), timeouts: { connect: 2000, response: 20000 } })

Cross-example notes: Show how to override per-route when hitting dedicated endpoints or when customers require low-latency single-request bursts (reduce pool, increase keepalive to avoid stale sockets).
telemetry_and_metrics: Collect: connection_acquire_latency_ms, connection_reuse_rate, idle_conn_count, socket_error_rate, streaming_chunk_latency_ms, stream_reconnect_count
SLOs: target connection_reuse_rate >= 85% for stable routes, socket_error_rate < 0.5% at p99 under normal load
testing_plan: Unit tests for timeouts and override precedence across SDK config layers
Integration tests using local env and a proxy that simulates TCP FIN, slow responses, and TLS handshake failures
Load test scenarios measuring connection churn and p99 latency with varied concurrency patterns (bursty vs steady)
Canary rollout by enabling new defaults for 10% of SDK-instantiated clients and monitor key metrics for 72 hours
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Longer default keepalive could hold file descriptors on low-resource hosts. Mitigation: document explicit lower-memory presets and add auto-prune after sustained idle period
Risk: Aggressive retries with long per-attempt timeouts can compound costs. Mitigation: default per-attempt timeout lower than overall deadline and add hedging cap
Risk: Language runtime differences (e.g., Node event loop vs Go scheduler) produce different tail behaviour. Mitigation: per-language tuned numeric defaults backed by microbenchmarks
rollout_and_communication: Merge handbook to SDK repo docs and release notes in sdk-2026.04
Developer-facing blog post and migration guide for advanced users
Update Console docs with a ‘SDK transport tuning’ how-to and links to presets for Dedicated customers
acceptance_criteria: Handbook merged in SDK mono-repo docs section with language examples and a short checklist
Automated tests covering override precedence and streaming timeout errors in CI
Canary metrics: connection_reuse_rate increased by >=10 percentage points for target routes; p99 latency not increased beyond 5%
At least one cross-team review (SDK leads + Platform Networking + Observability) completed and approvals recorded
